title: Remix Small Examples
description: Use these small Remix examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Choose browser rendering
examples.description: A single-page app loads a browser shell and lets routes choose its content.
examples.output: The framework builds an app intended to run its route work in the browser.

examples.title: Declare route files
examples.description: A route config maps addresses to route modules.
examples.output: The home module handles /, and the books module handles /books once those files are created.

examples.title: Write a route page
examples.description: A route module exports a component to show for its address.
examples.code:
// app/routes/home.tsx export default function Home(){return

Reading club

Choose a book today.

;}
examples.output: The home route shows a heading and paragraph.

examples.title: Use links for navigation
examples.description: Link changes the route while keeping the useful meaning of a link.
examples.output: The link opens the configured books route.

examples.title: Show a nested route
examples.description: A parent route can wrap child routes. Outlet is the place where the matched child appears.
examples.output: When this route has a matching child, the child is shown below Our books.

examples.title: Read an address parameter
examples.description: A route parameter captures a value from an address.
examples.output: At /books/moon-trip, the page shows Book: moon-trip.

examples.title: Load data in the browser
examples.description: clientLoader prepares route data in the browser.
examples.output: The route reads the real JSON file and shows one item per book.

examples.title: Show a first-load fallback
examples.description: A HydrateFallback can show a simple message while route data needed during initial hydration is loading.
examples.output: The fallback gives the reader a clear waiting message while that route prepares its initial client data.

examples.title: Give the active link a clear style
examples.description: NavLink knows whether its destination is the active route.
examples.code:
import {NavLink} from "react-router";
export default function Menu(){return <nav aria-label="Main"><NavLink to="/books" className={({isActive})=>isActive?"current":""}>Books</NavLink></nav>;}
examples.output: On the books route, the link receives the current class and active-page semantics.

examples.title: Use search values in the address
examples.description: Search parameters let a page keep small filter choices in the URL.
examples.code:
import {useSearchParams} from "react-router";
export default function Filter(){const [params,setParams]=useSearchParams();return <label>Topic <input value={params.get("topic")||""} onChange={e=>setParams({topic:e.target.value})}/></label>;}
examples.output: Typing changes the topic search value in the address as well as the input.

examples.title: Explain a route error
examples.description: A route ErrorBoundary can show a useful message when loading or rendering fails.
examples.output: A caught route error displays a clear message and a home link.

examples.title: Serve the browser build
examples.description: A browser route app needs its static host to return the app shell for supported client-side addresses.
examples.code:
Run the project build command.
Serve the generated build/client files.
Configure the static host fallback to index.html for client routes.
Open /books directly in a new tab.
Check that real asset requests still return their actual files.
examples.output: Both link navigation and direct route visits can open the app when the host fallback is correct.
